_meta.indication: GAZYVA, in combination with chlorambucil, is indicated for the treatment of patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, parallel-group, multicenter, randomized trial; stage 1a compared obinutuzumab + chlorambucil (GClb) vs chlorambucil (Clb) alone; conducted at 155 centers in 24 countries.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with previously untreated CD20+ CLL requiring treatment who had coexisting medical conditions or reduced renal function (CrCl <70 mL/min).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS); for regulatory decision based on Independent Review Committee (IRC) assessment.
pivotal_trials.n: N=356 in stage 1a: GClb n=238, Clb n=118.
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS by IRC 23.0 months (GClb) vs 11.1 months (Clb); HR 0.16 (95% CI 0.11, 0.24), p<0.0001. Overall response rate 75.9% vs 32.1%; complete response 27.8% vs 0.9%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5% and >=2% greater than chlorambucil): infusion related reactions (69%, Grade 3-4 21%), neutropenia (40%, Grade 3-4 34%), thrombocytopenia (15%, Grade 3-4 11%), anemia (12%), pyrexia (10%), cough (10%). Grade 3 or 4 tumor lysis syndrome occurred in 2%.
target_moa: Humanized anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (IgG1) that binds the CD20 antigen on pre-B and mature B-lymphocytes and mediates B-cell lysis through immune effector cell engagement (ADCC/ADCP), direct cell death, and complement activation.
modality: mAb (humanized anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, IgG1 subclass)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HEPATITIS B VIRUS REACTIVATION AND PROGRESSIVE MULTIFOCAL LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY — HBV reactivation (including fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, death) and PML, including fatal PML, can occur.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the biologic is not the first in its class, the trial design was acceptable, and no unexpected or controversial issues were raised.

description.text: Added updated efficacy and safety data from Study BO21004/CLL11 for obinutuzumab plus chlorambucil in previously untreated CLL patients with comorbidities

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for revisions to the US Prescribing Information (USPI) to include updated efficacy data and safety data based on the results of Stage 1a and primary Stage 2 analysis of Study BO21004/CLL11, "An Open-label, Multi-center, Three Arm Randomized, Phase 3 Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of RO5072759 + Chlorambucil (GClb), Rituximab + Chlorambucil (RClb) or Chlorambucil (Clb) Alone in Previously Untreated CLL Patients with Comorbidities".

description.text: Added indication for obinutuzumab (Gazyva) in combination with bendamustine followed by Gazyva monotherapy for follicular lymphoma relapsed/refractory to a rituximab-containing regimen

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication, which is Gazyva®, in combination with bendamustine followed by Gazyva® monotherapy, is indicated for the treatment of patients with follicular lymphoma (FL) who relapsed after, or are refractory to, a rituximab-containing regimen. The new indication is based on efficacy and safety data from the primary analysis of Study GAO4753g/GO01297 (GADOLIN), which evaluated obinutuzumab in combination with bendamustine followed by obinutuzumab monotherapy, compared with bendamustine alone in patients with indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma (iNHL) who did not respond to or progressed during or after treatment with rituximab or a rituximab-containing regimen.

description.text: Added new indication for GAZYVA in combination with chemotherapy, followed by monotherapy, for previously untreated stage II bulky, III or IV follicular lymphoma

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new indication for GAZYVA in combination with chemotherapy, followed by GAZYVA monotherapy in patients achieving at least a partial remission, for the treatment of adult patients with previously untreated stage II bulky, III or IV follicular lymphoma.

description.text: Updated labeling with GADOLIN (GAO4753) clinical efficacy results fulfilling postmarketing commitment #3048-2, with no new indication added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for revisions to section 14 (*Clinical Efficacy*) and section 6 (*Adverse Reactions*) of the US Prescribing Information (USPI) to include results from the clinical trial GAO4753 (GADOLIN), which addressed the postmarketing commitment #3048-2. The application also provides for the inclusion of Embryo-Fetal Toxicity in section 5 (*Warnings and Precautions*) of the USPI.

description.text: Added a new 90-minute (short duration) infusion dosing regimen for follicular lymphoma patients who tolerated 3 prior standard-rate administrations without Grade 3+ IRRs

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for a new dosing regimen: administration of obinutuzumab as an approximately 90-minute infusion in patients with follicular lymphoma who have completed 3 obinutuzumab administrations at the standard infusion rate without experiencing any Grade 3 or higher infusion related reactions (IRRs).

summary.text: BLA 125486 for obinutuzumab (GAZYVA) was received April 22, 2013 and reviewed as a priority review. Obinutuzumab received Breakthrough Therapy Designation and had orphan drug designation for CLL; approval was based on a single randomized phase 3 trial (BO21004/CLL11, stage 1a) demonstrating prolonged PFS.

citations.quote: The application was complete upon submission and was filed as a priority review. The PDUFA goal date for the current submission is December 22, 2013.

The applicant submitted a request to be designated as a Breakthrough Therapy and the designation was granted. The applicant has proposed the following indication: "for the treatment of patients with previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia".

Obinutuzumab was given orphan drug designation for the treatment of CLL on February 17, 2012 under the provisions of section 526 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Therefore, obinutuzumab is exempt from the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) requirement.

The clinical support for the proposed indication comes from a single randomized trial. Genentech conducted a single randomized, multi-center trial (BO21004/CLL11), entitled "An Open-label, Multi-center, Three Arm Randomized, Phase 3 Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of RO5072759 + Chlorambucil (GC1b), Rituximab + Chlorambucil (RC1b) or Chlorambucil (C1b) Alone in Previously Untreated CLL Pa"
